item.title: Flatbush Collapse Lawsuit: Tenant alleges landlord ignored cracks; claims remain unproven
item.description: In the wake of a devastating building collapse in Brooklyn that claimed eight lives, a musician has taken legal action against the landlord for ignoring warnings about visible cracks weeks prior. The lawsuit also raises alarms about nearby construction projects lacking proper structural support. Authorities are now probing the oversight of such projects in densely populated neighborhoods, questioning the responsiveness to residents' concerns before the tragic incident occurred.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
item.description: At a recent auction, a rare lock of George Washington’s hair sold for an impressive $4,000. This fascinating artifact once belonged to John Gadsby, who shared a meal with Washington shortly before his passing. Gadsby’s granddaughter later cherished the lock alongside a portrait of the first president, making it a remarkable piece of history. Notably, Washington's hair has previously commanded prices nearing $40,000 at auctions, alongside other treasured memorabilia.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: COP31 Talks Remain Divided: Countries review Turkish draft; climate support remains uncertain
item.description: At the COP31 climate conference in Turkey, urgent last-minute discussions are underway as Turkish officials unveil a draft agreement amid ongoing disputes regarding fossil fuels. Civil groups voice their frustration over the gradual pace of negotiations, demanding swift action on vital climate challenges. Nations most vulnerable to climate change are advocating for enhanced financial support for recovery and adaptation.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Asmongold's infamous house controversy returns after GTA 6 livestream with girlfriend Kaise
item.description: During a hilarious GTA 6 livestream, Asmongold and Kaise found themselves exploring a disheveled virtual home. Kaise jokingly compared the digital mess to Asmongold's real-life living situation, prompting laughs and nostalgia about Asmongold's cleanliness challenges. Even with improvements noted in 2026, his home remains a hot topic among viewers, fueling the ongoing chatter about his infamous house saga.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: IShowSpeed teases huge announcement after completing GTA 6 following 52-hour livestream
item.description: IShowSpeed celebrated a remarkable achievement by completing GTA 6's story mode in just 52 hours, far surpassing his initial plan of a 12-hour stream. His enthusiasm led him to extend the session, and upon finishing, he expressed heartfelt thanks and hinted at exciting future plans. Although a PS5 crash presented some obstacles, his progress was secure, keeping fans on the edge of their seats for his next move.

item.title: Arizona Appeals Court upholds son's 2015 property deed despite address error
item.description: In a complex legal battle over a Phoenix property, Robert Olsen asserted his ownership via a deed from 2015. His father's mistake in addressing the deed was countered by the accurate legal description, raising legal challenges. Following a transfer to a business entity in 2019, disputes escalated. Ultimately, the Arizona Court of Appeals affirmed Olsen's deed, nullifying subsequent transfers and clarifying his rightful ownership while clearing invalid records.

item.title: Lorri Cramer is known as the Turtle Lady of Manhattan and one summer she took in 680 babies
item.description: In the heart of Manhattan, Lorri Cramer, famously known as the Turtle Lady, dedicates her life to rescuing and rehabilitating injured and abandoned turtles. Her mission, not only to restore their health but also to secure safe environments for their future, has brought to light the troubling issue of non-native turtles being wrongfully released into inappropriate habitats.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Ohio landlord mistakenly throws away tenant's loved belongings; court upholds $6,000 award
item.description: Grace Davis was awarded $6,000 by an Ohio court after her landlord mistakenly discarded her personal belongings. Despite lacking receipts or photographs, she provided a detailed list with estimated values. The landlord's management company challenged the award, arguing that sufficient proof was missing. The appeals court upheld the ruling, stating that the unique nature of the items justified Davis's valuation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: More than 8,000 people applied to be NASA astronauts last time and just 10 were picked
item.description: NASA is currently accepting applications until December 3, 2026, for aspiring astronauts who dream of exploring outer space. To qualify, applicants must be U.S. citizens possessing a master's degree and relevant experience. Those with medical certifications or extensive flight backgrounds are particularly encouraged to apply. Selected astronauts will undergo rigorous training before embarking on missions to the Moon and Mars, with final candidates expected to be revealed by late 2027.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: An LA diner that served generations since 1924 shut down in 2025, has reopened under a nonprofit operator
item.description: After a lengthy shutdown in 2025 due to property issues, Original Pantry Cafe in Los Angeles has triumphantly reopened! With new management from Hope the Mission, the cafe will utilize its profits to bolster homelessness services. Diners can still indulge in the beloved classic menu while also enjoying fresh additions. Although hours have shifted, there are plans to bring back 24-hour service.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: As ice receded on a Swiss Alpine pass, archaeologists discovered a 4,000 years old bronze neck ring
item.description: A remarkable discovery at Lötschen Pass has unearthed a 4,000-year-old bronze neck ring, making it the first metal artifact found at this significant historical site. While previous discoveries were primarily organic materials preserved in ice, this find suggests that ancient peoples may have practiced mobility through Alpine passes, connecting various regions. Experts speculate that the ring could have served as a ritual offering or token of gratitude.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Indiana man paid $9,489 towards condo debt after $9,213 judgment, but court says he still owes more
item.description: Onnie James Florence Jr. encountered significant legal troubles stemming from his failure to pay homeowners' association fees for his condominium in Indiana. After acquiring the unit, he neglected to keep up with payments while residing in Illinois. The Meridian Arch Owners Association successfully secured a default judgment against him for the overdue fees. Despite making a partial payment later, additional fees remained unpaid, prompting ongoing legal action.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dua Lipa's £6.75 million London home renovation set to finish in 2027
item.description: Dua Lipa is making waves with the transformation of her Victorian home in Hampstead, which includes an ambitious plan for a luxurious basement pool. After encountering numerous setbacks, the project received the green light to commence construction in 2024. Local environmental concerns have prompted strict adherence to regulations, pushing the anticipated completion to 2027. With an investment estimated at around £3 million, this renovation underscores its intricate and grand vision.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
